bull_argument.argument:
Solarvest's RM2.371bn unbilled order book creates a concrete revenue-conversion opportunity, complemented by electricity-sales growth of 25.8%. Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, profit 19.8%, and net margin improved from 11.5% to 12.2%. These observations support the case that delivered projects and recurring electricity activity can build earnings beyond a single headline.

The order book is not cash, and 89.1% EPCC exposure makes timing and execution central. Sequential revenue fell from RM270.5m, while debt and FCF remain unknown. Stable domestic policy is useful financing context, not a verified subsidy catalyst. The intact uptrend supports interest, but RSI above 82 and weak volume mean a bullish long-term scenario does not establish an attractive immediate entry.
key_points: Profit outgrew revenue and reported margin improved.
Order book and electricity sales offer different potential growth channels.
EPCC conversion, funding and overbought pricing remain the key hurdles.

bear_argument.argument:
Solarvest's RM2.371bn backlog is a credible opportunity, but 89.1% EPCC exposure concentrates execution and cash-conversion risk. Revenue declined sequentially from RM270.5m to RM155.9m despite 13.2% year-on-year growth. The observed 12.2% net margin improvement does not establish that future project timing and margins will be stable.

Electricity-sales growth of 25.8% is constructive, yet it does not make the larger project book recurring cash. Debt and FCF remain unknown and the vendor trailing multiple is 48.00x. RSI above 82 with a five-bar pullback and below-average volume makes chasing especially difficult. A project-delay or cost-overrun downside is an execution scenario, not an observed new disruption.
key_points: Backlog is not cash; EPCC dominates exposure.
Sequential revenue contraction qualifies annual growth.
Funding evidence and near-term entry confirmation are incomplete.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull correctly identifies a growth runway, but its recurring-electricity argument does not neutralise 89.1% EPCC exposure. The sequential revenue decline demonstrates timing variability already present in the evidence; backlog size alone cannot establish profitable funded delivery.

bull_argument.argument:
The bear's sequential-revenue counterexample demonstrates project timing variability, but annual revenue growth and a higher reported net margin show that the latest lower-volume quarter still earned more than its year-earlier counterpart. This does not establish stable future margins. It does mean the supplied evidence supports profitable execution in the observed quarter rather than merely a large undelivered book.

Electricity-sales growth is a secondary opportunity, not a claim that the 89.1% EPCC exposure has become recurring. The prospective upside is continued profitable backlog delivery, with electricity activity adding another channel. Unknown debt and FCF keep the financing challenge open, and the stretched chart and 48.00x vendor multiple make chasing difficult. The bear identifies the conditions for successful execution, without evidence here of an actual new delay or cost overrun.
key_points: Observed annual profit growth and margin expansion counter a purely backlog-led thesis.
Sequential variability is real and future conversion remains conditional.
Electricity growth complements EPCC rather than eliminating its risk.
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The RM270.5m-to-RM155.9m sequential decline does show variability, but 13.2% year-on-year revenue growth, 19.8% profit growth and margin expansion to 12.2% show the observed quarter remained productive. That rebuts treating timing variability itself as proof of failed profitable delivery, while funding remains unknown.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's strongest refinement is profitable year-on-year execution in the latest quarter, rather than backlog alone. Revenue growth of 13.2%, profit growth of 19.8% and margin of 12.2% genuinely establish that point. They do not answer how the RM2.371bn backlog will translate into financed cash returns when 89.1% exposure remains EPCC and debt/FCF are unknown.

Sequential revenue declining from RM270.5m to RM155.9m demonstrates variable delivery, not failed projects. A buyer at the 48.00x vendor multiple must nevertheless accept uncertain timing and cash conversion without evidence of financing adequacy. Electricity-sales growth complements the book but does not neutralise its dominant exposure. The extended chart adds entry caution; waiting needs no assertion of a new delay or cost overrun.
key_points: Future backlog cash conversion and funding are unanswered.
EPCC concentration and extended pricing constrain immediate entry.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: Annual profit growth answers a purely undelivered-backlog objection. It does not rebut the financing and timing concern; the bull explicitly leaves both open, so observed quarterly profitability alone is insufficient to justify buying.

bull_case_summary: Solarvest delivered year-on-year revenue and profit growth with higher net margin, alongside a substantial backlog and growing electricity sales. Round two emphasises actual profitable execution rather than backlog alone, while keeping purchase conviction conditional on funded conversion.
bear_case_summary: Dominant EPCC exposure and the large sequential revenue decline show delivery timing sensitivity. Round two accepts quarterly profitability but notes that unknown debt and FCF leave backlog cash conversion unverified, with a premium snapshot multiple and extended chart.
key_points_of_agreement: Backlog is neither cash nor guaranteed future earnings.
Electricity sales do not neutralise dominant EPCC exposure.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether profitable quarterly delivery adequately counters timing and financing risk for a prospective purchase.
unresolved_uncertainties: Debt and FCF adequacy for backlog delivery.
Repeatability of margins through variable project timing.
Matched valuation and sustainable entry conditions; no new delay or cost overrun is established.
